source: CARDI book "ដំណាំស្រូវនៅកម្ពុជា" (Rice Cultivation in Cambodia), by Men Sarom, Thuy Lina and Pheng Thimuny, published by CARDI, 2007, Chapter 7 (Rice-based farming systems), by Phal Sovuthy, Chan Phaloeun, Ung Sopheap and Nath Sarouny. No elibrary URL visible.
text: National-level economic context for rice-based farming in Cambodia (background rather than a technique). Agriculture accounted for roughly 37.6% of Cambodia's GDP (NIS, 2001 figure cited in the source), and about 80% of the rural population's livelihood depends on rice-based farming systems (Royal Government of Cambodia, 2004). Around 2.2 million households were growing rice nationally, with a national average landholding of roughly 0.9 hectares per household (citing Nesbitt, 1997 and Ouk et al., 2001). The source frames Cambodian rice-based farming systems as shaped by three main factors: (1) the physical/agroecological environment (soil, water availability, flood/drought risk), (2) socioeconomic conditions of the farm household (labor availability, capital, market access), and (3) government policy and institutional support (extension services, credit, infrastructure). A cited framework (Singh, 2000) identifies farm household objectives and resource constraints as the key determinants of which farming-system combination (rice alone vs. rice plus livestock, home garden, cash crops, or fishing) a given household adopts. As a household-level illustration (not a national average), the source presents a multi-year income-diversification table from a CARDI research-station demonstration household model, covering 1998-2003 income by source in thousand riel: fruit/garden crop income, other/mixed cash crop income, rice income, and livestock income, with garden/orchard and livestock income shown growing over the period relative to a relatively flat rice-income contribution - illustrating a general strategy of diversifying beyond rice-only farming for income growth, rather than precise figures meant to be read as a national benchmark.
caveat: The household-level income table (CARDI's own research-station demonstration table 7-2) is presented here in qualitative/directional terms only rather than transcribed figure-by-figure, since it is a small, dense multi-year table read via page rasterization, and it explicitly describes a single research-station demonstration model rather than a broader farmer sample - readers should not treat it as a representative national income breakdown. The three headline national statistics (37.6% of GDP, 80% of rural population, ~2.2 million households, ~0.9 ha/household average) come from the source's clearly-legible prose text and are considered more reliable than the table figures. All of these statistics reflect conditions as of the early-to-mid 2000s (this book was published in 2007) and should be treated as historical context rather than current figures.
